sourceNote: Reviewed all supplied events, E0–E1875. The transcript contains recognition errors and events spanning speaker changes; inseparably mixed events are marked U. Attribution follows conversational turns rather than ideological content. No edited teaser replay was identified. One genuinely uncertain protection episode is recorded; no unsupported slogan is confirmed.

candidates.speaker: A
candidates.quote: that just doesn't do anything to render it likely that on naturalism
candidates.explanation: Craig denies that failures explain successful mathematical precision (E1094–1106), potentially sidelining Oppy's selection-effect objection (E1070–1084). But he acknowledges failures and supplies an infinite-mathematics/finite-world rationale (E1085–1093). Whether he excludes relevant counterevidence regardless of merits or disputes its explanatory relevance remains unclear; this is an ordinary argument, not an unsupported affirmation.

contrasts.speaker: A
contrasts.quote: they are true within a certain range
contrasts.explanation: Craig limits classical mechanics to approximate accuracy within a domain, disclaims a final formulation, and illustrates degrees of precision with clocks. This supplies an explicit qualification and analogy rather than simply repeating that mathematics works.

contrasts.speaker: B
contrasts.quote: it had to be because it had to be
contrasts.explanation: Despite its slogan-like wording, this summarizes explicitly stated modal assumptions (E1143–1177). Oppy subsequently makes the theory answerable to comparative explanatory virtues and total evidence (E1240–1277), rather than treating necessity as automatic public proof.
